messages:
maya_support: FYI ACME is escalating — streaming calls are aborting mid-response. They get a client-side 'Broken pipe' / ECONNRESET and our billing/metrics are tagging the request as a 5xx. They're seeing charged tokens and want a refund. I opened INC-7941. Request IDs: r-3f8a9c, r-3f8a9d. Posting minimal repro and headers they shared.

maya_support: curl example they used:
```bash
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\n  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\n  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-4b","prompt":"stream test","stream":true}'
```

maya_support: customer logs show repeated `write: broken pipe` on their client around mid-stream and gateway logs show `upstream reset` for the same request ids. Billing classified them as 5xx because gateway saw upstream connection failure.

eriq_eng: thanks @maya_support :wave: can you paste the gateway request_id and the exact upstream error lines from our edge logs? need to see if it's client-close or upstream crash. Also which AZ/region?

maya_support: region us-east-1a. Edge snippets for r-3f8a9c:
```
[2026-03-16T14:02:11.234Z] edge: request_id=r-3f8a9c route=/v1/generate client_ip=34.12.9.7
[2026-03-16T14:02:12.120Z] proxy: upstream_conn_reset request_id=r-3f8a9c reason=ECONNRESET from=10.2.5.11:443
[2026-03-16T14:02:12.121Z] billing: mark_5xx request_id=r-3f8a9c code=502 note=upstream_reset
```

sam_sre: That pattern often means the client closed the socket while the upstream was mid-chunk. In some cases the proxy sees the upstream `RST` and attributes blame to upstream (5xx). We should confirm whether the client sent FIN first. Do we have tcpdump from the edge?

maya_support: I pulled tcpdump capture from the customer side (they attached). Key snippet shows client FIN at 14:02:12.119 then server RST at 14:02:12.120. So the sequence looks like client halfclose then proxy reset.

zane_repro: I reproduced locally with a tiny script — if client stops reading for >150ms while server is mid-chunk, our proxy appears to close upstream and labels as 5xx. Repro script: 
```py
import requests, time
r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer ...'}, json={'model':'rwd-4b','stream':True}, stream=True)
for i,chunk in enumerate(r.iter_content(chunk_size=None)):
    print('got', i)
    if i==3:
        time.sleep(0.18)  # trigger client-side pause -> broken pipe
        break
```

zane_repro: confirms proxy behavior. On our side the metric `proxy.upstream_resets` increments and billing heuristics map that -> 5xx.

eriq_eng: ok — we need two things: (1) short-term: classify resets where tcp trace shows client FIN before upstream RST as `client_abort` (not billable 5xx) so support can credit. (2) longer-term: adjust proxy halfclose handling so we don't aggressively reset upstream on transient client stalls. I can draft a PR for the classification change — will need a deployment window.

sam_sre: agree. I'll open a telemetry patch to emit a new label `termination_reason=client_halfclose` with request_id. Also add a debug flag to keep the chunked state for 30s to see if it's transient.

maya_support: tagging @eriq_eng and @sam_sre on INC-7941. I've told the customer we're investigating and we may issue a credit pending the classification rule.

eriq_eng: creating internal ticket INFRA-5129 for the heuristic change. Plan: emit non-billable event for existing requests that match (client FIN -> upstream RST) and backfill credits for last 48h for matching request_ids. Will need approval from finance for backfill.

maya_support: finance looped in on INC-7941. Customer asked for ETA. What's realistic?

eriq_eng: quick patch for classification and telemetry in canary within 24-36h if nothing funky shows during testing. Longer fix for proxy behavior is a couple weeks.

sam_sre: I'll prepare runbook steps for support to check tcpdump and proxy trace quickly: step 1) look for client FIN timestamp, step 2) check `proxy.upstream_conn_reset` after FIN, step 3) if matches, mark non-billable. Putting that runbook in the ticket now.

maya_support: great. I've posted the customer-facing note in the ticket and scheduled a follow-up call. cc'ing @deploy-bot to watch the canary job.

deploy-bot: Canary pipeline started for INFRA-5129 classification change (job id: canary-7789). Notifying on progress.

eriq_eng: thanks all. I'll follow up here with canary results and a suggested credit list. :thumbsup:
